#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Finish-the-corpus ingestion: ALL remaining repos + op-dbus-proto + compliance
# → the voyage-4 shared space / Qdrant. Run this yourself (no Claude tokens).
#
# Covers:
#   • remaining Rust deps (44), Java (1), specs_docs (3)   ← finish prior runs
#   • compliance corpus (recovered repos + industry templates + in-tree docs)
#   • op-dbus-proto (this repo)
#
# Token safety:
#   • ALREADY-EMBEDDED repos are skipped via per-repo done-files
#     (logs/vector-state/<collection>.<repo>.done) — no re-embed, no re-spend.
#     A preflight prints how many are already done per collection.
#   • Budget caps = the CURRENT remaining free balance per key (net of prior
#     usage), in FRESH budget files so stale 'used' counts don't mis-account.
#   • MODEL+KEY rotation: the whole voyage-4 trio shares one embedding space, so
#     when a (model,key) balance depletes (pipeline exits 75) we rotate to the
#     next tier and resume — vectors still fuse into the same collections, no
#     re-index. KeyPool rotates keys within a tier; this loop rotates models.
#
# What it does NOT do (free, no-token follow-up = the Rust enrich tool):
#   Cozo population + canonical control_refs (set_payload) + OSCAL control nodes.
#
# PREREQS: Qdrant up on :6333 · ~/.bash_secrets has VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST &
#          VOYAGE_API_KEY_LITE · ~/git/.venv-vectorize present.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
set -uo pipefail

ROOT=/home/jeremy/git
PY=$ROOT/.venv-vectorize/bin/python
REPOS=$ROOT/repos
LSP=$ROOT/lsp
LOG_DIR=$ROOT/logs
STATE_DIR=$LOG_DIR/vector-state
OPDBUS=$ROOT/operation-dbus-proto
QDRANT_URL=${QDRANT_URL:-http://localhost:6333}
DIM=1024
BATCH=${BATCH:-24}

TS=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
LOG=$LOG_DIR/ingest_all_$TS.log
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR" "$REPOS" "$LSP" "$STATE_DIR" "$REPOS/_local"
ln -sfn "$LOG" "$LOG_DIR/ingest_all.latest.log"
log() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$*" | tee -a "$LOG"; }

# ── model tiers: "model|key_envs(cap=current free remaining)|budget_file" ─────
# Caps come straight from the dashboard balances you pasted (already net of
# prior spend). Fresh budget files (…-r2…) so old 'used' totals aren't inherited.
MODEL_TIERS=(
  "voyage-4|VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST:195000000,VOYAGE_API_KEY_LITE:195000000|$LOG_DIR/voyage-4-budget.json"
  "voyage-4-large|VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST:4000000,VOYAGE_API_KEY_LITE:65000000|$LOG_DIR/voyage-4-large-r2-budget.json"
  "voyage-4-lite|VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST:45000000|$LOG_DIR/voyage-4-lite-r2-budget.json"
)

# ── groups: "name|list-file|collection|max-file-bytes" ───────────────────────
GROUPS=(
  "lsp_rust|$LOG_DIR/lsp_rust_remaining.txt|repos_lsp_rust_voyage_4_large|2000000"
  "lsp_java|$LOG_DIR/lsp_java_voyage_4_lite_remaining.safe.txt|repos_lsp_java_voyage_4_lite|2000000"
  "specs_docs|$LOG_DIR/specs_docs_voyage_4_lite_remaining.safe.txt|repos_specs_docs_voyage_4_lite|20000000"
  "compliance|$LSP/compliance.txt|compliance_voyage_4|20000000"
  "op_dbus|$LSP/op_dbus_proto.txt|op_dbus_proto_voyage_4|2000000"
)

# ── compliance corpora + industry-DECLARED templates (explicit URLs) ─────────
declare -A REPO_URLS=(
  ["LINCnil/GDPR-Developer-Guide"]="https://github.com/LINCnil/GDPR-Developer-Guide"
  ["compl-ai/compl-ai"]="https://github.com/compl-ai/compl-ai"
  ["TechShieldOlamide/trustgrid-compliance-templates"]="https://github.com/TechShieldOlamide/trustgrid-compliance-templates"
  ["vaibhavjain2608/compliance-policy-templates"]="https://github.com/vaibhavjain2608/compliance-policy-templates"
  ["Auxin-io/cybersecurity-templates"]="https://github.com/Auxin-io/cybersecurity-templates"
)

export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
clone_one() {  # name url  — skip if already present
  local name="$1" url="$2" dest="$REPOS/$1"
  if [ -d "$dest/.git" ]; then return 0; fi
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
  log "clone $name"
  git clone --depth 1 "$url" "$dest" >>"$LOG" 2>&1 || log "  CLONE FAILED: $url"
}
clone_list() {  # clone any github org/repo in a list-file that's missing
  local list="$1"; [ -f "$list" ] || return 0
  while IFS= read -r repo; do
    repo=$(echo "$repo" | xargs); [ -z "$repo" ] && continue
    [ -d "$REPOS/$repo/.git" ] && continue

Confirmed your hypothesis — and with a nuance. The `unix_socket` plugin projection is **`{"sockets":[]}`** — empty. So `create_unix_socket` has **not** been run for netmaker (the shared socket has zero registered names). You're right.

The nuance: it's empty for **every** container — `netmaker-mq`/`netmaker-ui` aren't registered either, yet they run. So "not registered" alone doesn't explain why netmaker *fails to start* (that crash is in Incus/LXC, before the app, so before any socket demux matters). The concrete config difference between netmaker (fails) and netmaker-ui (works) is:

| | netmaker (STOPPED) | netmaker-ui (RUNNING) |
|---|---|---|
| image | oci | oci |
| socket path | `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock` | same |
| **`security.privileged`** | **`true`** (idmap `[]`) | unset → **unprivileged** (real idmap) |

So the `/run` tmpfs `EINVAL` tracks with **netmaker being privileged** — a privileged OCI container's `/run` tmpfs mount fails where the unprivileged one succeeds. The socket-under-`/run` is identical on both and isn't the trigger (ui proves it).

So there are really two separate things, and your instinct points at the fix for one of them:
1. **Provision netmaker's socket the right way** — run `createunixsocket` for it (via the plugin method / `zbusctl createsocket --name netmaker --port 8081,1883 --path /run/ghostbridge/container.sock`), same as the others should be. This is correct regardless.
2. **The start-crash** is most likely the **`security.privileged: true`** on the OCI container, not the socket. netmaker-ui (unprivileged) starts; netmaker (privileged) hits the `/run` EINVAL.

So before we declare the socket the cause: do you want netmaker to be **privileged**? If it doesn't truly need it (ui doesn't), dropping `security.privileged` likely lets `/run` mount and the container start — then we run `createunixsocket` for it on top. Want me to (a) run the `createunixsocket` provisioning for netmaker, and/or (b) test the start with `security.privileged` cleared?

content.text:
That's the right question to be asking, and it cuts deeper than the socket bug. Let me separate the principle from the current breakage.

## The principle: yes — one identity-gated surface
Right now there are two doors:
- **System bus** → `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` (projection, **reads**) — gated only by D-Bus policy (uid/peer), **not** by the Ghostbridge footprint.
- **Session bus** (`/run/op-dbus/session-bus.sock`) → `org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp` → MutationEngine (**writes**) — this is where the **wristband/footprint** is actually enforced.

So today the **write path is footprint-gated and the read path isn't.** Per [[project_zero_trust_principle]], the wristband is supposed to be the *only* gate — "IP ACLs, firewall rules, port restrictions are theater." An ungated read surface that anything on the box can scrape is the same kind of theater hole: it leaks present-state (plugin configs, identities, topology) without ever presenting a footprint. So **if a consumer crosses the trust boundary, it should come through the identity-gated surface — reads included.** That argues for consolidating onto the gated (session/cognitive) door, exactly as you're saying.

## The one legitimate exception (scope it tightly)
The identity gate is enforced *at ingress* by the interceptor. A system-bus projection is acceptable **only** for consumers that are provably **same-host, already-behind-the-gate, and trusted** (e.g. `projection_serv` feeding op-web locally, which itself sits behind xray/xraqy). The test is concrete: *does any untrusted or cross-boundary caller read `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` directly?* If yes → it must move behind the footprint. If it's only internal plumbing that never faces an external peer, system bus is a local convenience, not a hole. I won't claim "all reads must move" as a blanket — it depends on who consumes the projection, which is checkable.

So the principled end state: **one footprint-gated surface for anything crossing the boundary** (reads served through the same gate as writes), and the system bus demoted to verified-internal-only — or removed.

## But note: the gated door is itself broken right now
The session-bus mutation backend just gave `BrokenPipe` — `org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp` accepted the connection and dropped the call. So even the *correct* gated path isn't serving `createsocket` at the moment. That's an orthogonal bug from the architecture decision: consolidating everything onto the session bus only helps once that backend actually responds.

Two threads, your call on order:
1. **Architecture**: I record this (single footprint-gated surface; audit who reads the system-bus projection; plan to move reads behind the gate) — want it in SIGNALS as a decision/concern?
2. **Unblock now**: debug why `org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp` drops the `createsocket` call (its log / whether it even owns the name on that session bus), since that's what's stopping the socket provisioning you asked for.

Which first — or both?

Correct — but they clear two different bars, and it's worth being precise about which:

- **The backend fix is unconditional.** `org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp` dropping the `createsocket` call means the *gated mutation door doesn't serve at all* right now. Nothing that goes through the MutationEngine works until that's fixed — no socket provisioning, no plugin mutations, no `createunixsocket`. That's "functional at all," not a nicety.

- **The single-gate consolidation is what makes it "as advertised."** The system is sold on [[project_zero_trust_principle]] — the wristband as the *only* gate. A working write-gate plus a parallel ungated system-bus read surface isn't that model; it's "mostly Zero Trust." So to match the advertising, the gate has to both **work** and **be the only door across the boundary.**

The one place I won't overstate: whether the consolidation is *required* vs. *hardening* hinges on a checkable fact — **does anything untrusted/cross-boundary actually read `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` directly?** If the only readers are trusted same-host plumbing already behind xray/xraqy, you're "as advertised" and consolidation is defense-in-depth. If an external peer can reach it, it's a real hole and required. That audit decides it — not a blanket claim.

So: **both, in dependency order.** Fix the gated backend first (unblocks everything immediately and is unconditional), then audit the projection's consumers and consolidate/move reads behind the gate.

"Functional as advertised" end-to-end means that whole chain has to be real: **gated backend serving → socket passthrough → netmaker up → qdrant reachable → vectorize + Cozo → the plugins the frontend calls.** Each link we've found broken is one stop on that chain.

You're right, and that's the deeper bug — my "just update the constants" was a band-aid that would drift again the next rename. Hardcoding the service/object/interface in zbusctl **defeats the entire point of a projected, introspectable tree.** The projection *is* the discovery mechanism; a client should resolve the address from it, not bake a copy that silently rots — which is exactly what happened (zbusctl froze `org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp` / `/org/opdbus/v1/cognitive` before the `.v1.plugins` naming, and nothing told it the world moved).

This is the **same disease as everything else this session**: a derived value duplicated away from its single source —
- the hardcoded `load_plugin` dispatch table → replaced with inventory discovery,
- reflection advertising a surface that didn't match what's mounted → one shared route-builder,
- the canonical map → kept in the doc, not copied to a json,
- and now zbusctl's names → should be **read from the projected tree**, not frozen.

The precise principle (not "zero hardcoding" — that's impossible): **hardcode only the one stable root anchor; discover everything below it.** zbusctl is allowed to know `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` (the entry point). It is *not* allowed to hardcode the leaf — the object path, the interface, the version suffix. Those it should walk/introspect from the tree. It hardcoded the leaf, which is exactly the part that drifts.

And there's a second layer to it: `createsocket` is a **plugin mutation** (`createunixsocket` on the `unix_socket` plugin). The architecturally-correct zbusctl shouldn't target a bespoke `cognitive` object at all — it should route through the **generic mutation surface** (`PluginService.CallMethod{plugin_id="unix_socket", method="createunixsocket"}`), the single MutationEngine authority you've been pointing me at all along. That path is rename-proof *and* plugin-agnostic: zbusctl wouldn't need to know about `cognitive_mcp` or any specific object — just "call this method on this plugin," resolved against the live tree.

So the right fix is two changes, not one:
1. **zbusctl discovers from the projection** (anchor on the root well-known name, introspect to the target) instead of hardcoding the object/interface/version.
2. **Route the mutation through the generic CallMethod** (unix_socket/createunixsocket), not a hardcoded cognitive endpoint — so it goes through the one gated mutation door we discussed, and survives any future rename.

Want me to rewrite `zbusctl createsocket` that way — discover-and-CallMethod instead of hardcoded names? That's the fix that actually matches "project the tree."

# Factory task: make the op-dbus projected D-Bus tree deterministic (start with zbusctl)

Use agent orchestration. Goal: eliminate hardcoded D-Bus addressing so the projected
tree is the single source of truth, then enforce it with checks (a convention already
rotted once). Start with the concrete zbusctl bug, then the four determinism conditions.

## Repos
- Backplane / plugins / projection: `/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto` (Rust workspace)
- Client CLI (separate repo): `/home/jeremy/git/zbusctl`

## Principle (the architectural law)
The system exposes a self-describing, introspectable **projected D-Bus tree** rooted at the
well-known name `org.opdbus.v1.plugins`, plus a **gated mutation path** (MutationEngine via
`PluginService.CallMethod`, enforced by the Ghostbridge interceptor: requires
`x-ghostbridge-footprint` + `x-ghostbridge-trace-id`). Consumers must **DISCOVER** addresses
from the tree (introspection). They must **NOT hardcode** object paths, interfaces, or version
suffixes. Hardcoding only the single stable root anchor is allowed; everything below it is
discovered. A hardcoded leaf is a frozen snapshot that silently diverges on rename.

## The concrete bug (proximate, start here)
`zbusctl createsocket` (`/home/jeremy/git/zbusctl/src/main.rs`, ~lines 163-165) targets names
that no longer exist:
- service `org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp`  · object `/org/opdbus/v1/cognitive` · interface `org.opdbus.CognitiveMcpV1`  ← ALL WRONG

The real served names (source of truth:
`operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-cognitive-mcp/src/dbus_interface.rs` lines 3-5 and 27):
- service `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` · object `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/cognitive_mcp` · interface `org.opdbus.v1.plugins.CognitiveMcp`

Result: `zbusctl createsocket` fails `ServiceUnknown` (system bus) / `BrokenPipe` (session bus).
It predates the `.v1.plugins` rename and rotted silently because the path was never exercised
(the `unix_socket` plugin projection shows `{"sockets":[]}` — `createunixsocket` has never run
for any container).

## Primary task — rewrite `zbusctl createsocket`
1. Hardcode ONLY the stable root anchor (`org.opdbus.v1.plugins`); DISCOVER the object path,
   interface, and method by introspecting the projected tree.
2. Route socket creation through the GENERIC mutation surface —
   `PluginService.CallMethod{plugin_id="unix_socket", method="createunixsocket"}` (the single
   gated MutationEngine authority) — NOT a bespoke `cognitive` object/interface. Rename-proof
   and plugin-agnostic.
3. Connect to the correct bus and honor auth. The op-dbus **session bus** is
   `unix:path=/run/op-dbus/session-bus.sock` and requires **root**; the system-bus projection
   `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` is owned by `projection_serv`. Determine + document which bus the
   mutation path uses.

Backend reference: `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/unix_socket.rs::create_unix_socket(name, ports)`
binds the shared host socket `SHARED_CONTAINER_SOCKET = /run/ghostbridge/container.sock` and
registers `name` as the demux tag. Validation target: provision netmaker =
`--name netmaker --path /run/ghostbridge/container.sock --port 8081,1883`.

## Broader goal — 4 conditions for a DETERMINISTIC projected tree (SIGNALS OD-31)
Each was observed broken this session. Make each true AND enforced by a check:
1. ONE producer derived from one source.
2. Reliably refreshed to present-state ON READ. (Observed stale: projection reported
   `qdrant: unavailable / dimensions 1536` and `netmaker: Stopped` lagging reality.)
3. Each well-known name UNAMBIGUOUSLY OWNED. (Observed: `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` owned by
   `projection_serv` on the SYSTEM bus AND `ovs-dbus-init` on the SESSION bus.)
4. EVERY consumer DISCOVERS from the tree — zero hardcoded leaves. (zbusctl is one; audit ALL.)

## Acceptance criteria (CHECKS, not conventions)
- A CI/lint or Rust integration test that FAILS if any backplane consumer hardcodes a D-Bus
  object path, interface, or version suffix. Only the root well-known name
  `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` may appear as a literal.
- A check that each well-known name has exactly one owner per bus.
- `zbusctl createsocket --name netmaker --path /run/ghostbridge/container.sock --port 8081,1883`
  succeeds end-to-end (when the backend is up) via discovery + CallMethod, and the `unix_socket`
  plugin projection then lists `netmaker`.
- No regression to the Ghostbridge-gated mutation path.

## Suggested sub-agent orchestration
- **Agent A — zbusctl rewrite**: discover-from-tree + CallMethod; delete hardcoded leaves;
  `cargo build` + `cargo clippy` clean.
- **Agent B — consumer audit + the check**: grep both repos for hardcoded `org.opdbus.*` object
  paths / interfaces / version suffixes; list them; fix or file follow-ups; author the
  lint/test that enforces "no hardcoded leaves".
- **Agent C — name ownership**: why `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` is double-owned (system vs session
  bus), and why `op-cognitive-mcp` isn't connected to the session bus / doesn't claim its name;
  implement single-owner resolution.
- **Agent D — projection freshness**: make knowledge/incus projections reflect present-state on
  read (the stale qdrant/netmaker statuses); reconcile the reactive refresh.
- **Verifier**: run the checks; confirm createsocket end-to-end; open SIGNALS follow-ups for
  anything deferred.

## Conventions / guardrails
- Single source of truth; no hardcoding. Same class as recent fixes: inventory self-registration
  replaced a hardcoded plugin dispatch table; one shared gRPC route-builder so reflection matches
  the served surface (SIGNALS OD-29).
- Do NOT break the gated mutation path (Ghostbridge interceptor headers).
- Keep commits scoped; follow each repo's commit conventions.
- Note: knowledge plugin config was just corrected to `dimensions=1024 / provider=voyage /
  model=voyage-4` in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/knowledge_plugin.rs` (needs
  `projection_serv` redeploy to show live) — don't revert it.
- Append observations/decisions to `operation-dbus-proto/SIGNALS.md` (OD-31 is the tracking row).

  Findings from reconnaissance

   /org/opdbus/v1/cognitive / org.opdbus.CognitiveMcpV1 and routes through CallTool("cognitive_memory", )  so it's doubly wrong: 
   dead names and it stores a memory record instead of ever reaching the unix_socket plugin or the gated MutationEngine.

   One premise in the prompt is wrong, and the prompt asked me to determine it. "Which bus does the mutation path use?" Answer: none
     the gated mutation path is gRPC, not D-Bus.

     PluginService.CallMethod (operation.proto:41)  MutationEngine.mutate(ChangeType::MethodCall) already dispatches 
      plugin_id="unix_socket", method="createunixsocket"  UnixSocketPlugin::create_unix_socket(name, ports). (mutation_engine.rs)
     That gRPC surface is mounted by build_operation_routes on op-dbus TCP :50051 and the zeroclaw bridge :8090 + 
      /run/ghostbridge/container.sock, all behind ghostbridge_interceptor (requires x-ghostbridge-footprint + x-ghostbridge-trace-id
       matching the live identity sled).
     The D-Bus projected tree org.opdbus.v1.plugins (projection/dbus_server.rs) serves read-only ProjectedObject properties + an 
      updated signal. There is no `CallMethod` / mutation on D-Bus. It's a discovery surface only.
     zbusctl is a pure `zbus` client (no tonic). So "discover from the D-Bus tree, then call PluginService.CallMethod" inherently 
      means zbusctl must bridge both transports.

   Consumer audit (hardcoded leaves) is large and real. Besides zbusctl, hardcoded interface/path literals live in 
   op-web/src/projection_client.rs, op-web/src/state_manager_client.rs, op-tools/.../plugin_projection.rs + 
   discovery/projection_engine.rs, op-openvswitch-daemon/.../ovs_attach.rs (legacy /plugin/plugins/ paths), and 
   op-chat/src/grpc_client.rs (interface_name: "org.opdbus.AgentV1"). A canonical helper already exists 
   (op_plugins::canonical::plugin_path()), so the enforcement check + migration target is well-defined.

    createsocket validation (acceptance #3) can't be executed by me now  I can make it correct + buildable + unit/lint-checked and

# Factory task: make the op-dbus projected D-Bus tree deterministic (start with zbusctl)

Use agent orchestration. Goal: eliminate hardcoded D-Bus addressing so the projected
tree is the single source of truth, then enforce it with checks (a convention already
rotted once). Start with the concrete zbusctl bug, then the four determinism conditions.

## Repos
- Backplane / plugins / projection: `/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto` (Rust workspace)
- Client CLI (separate repo): `/home/jeremy/git/zbusctl`

## Principle (the architectural law)
The system exposes a self-describing, introspectable **projected D-Bus tree** rooted at the
well-known name `org.opdbus.v1.plugins`, plus a **gated mutation path** (MutationEngine via
`PluginService.CallMethod`, enforced by the Ghostbridge interceptor: requires
`x-ghostbridge-footprint` + `x-ghostbridge-trace-id`). Consumers must **DISCOVER** addresses
from the tree (introspection). They must **NOT hardcode** object paths, interfaces, or version
suffixes. Hardcoding only the single stable root anchor is allowed; everything below it is
discovered. A hardcoded leaf is a frozen snapshot that silently diverges on rename.

## The concrete bug (proximate, start here)
`zbusctl createsocket` (`/home/jeremy/git/zbusctl/src/main.rs`, ~lines 163-165) targets names
that no longer exist:
- service `org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp`  · object `/org/opdbus/v1/cognitive` · interface `org.opdbus.CognitiveMcpV1`  ← ALL WRONG

The real served names (source of truth:
`operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-cognitive-mcp/src/dbus_interface.rs` lines 3-5 and 27):
- service `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` · object `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/cognitive_mcp` · interface `org.opdbus.v1.plugins.CognitiveMcp`

Result: `zbusctl createsocket` fails `ServiceUnknown` (system bus) / `BrokenPipe` (session bus).
It predates the `.v1.plugins` rename and rotted silently because the path was never exercised
(the `unix_socket` plugin projection shows `{"sockets":[]}` — `createunixsocket` has never run
for any container).

## Primary task — rewrite `zbusctl createsocket`
1. Hardcode ONLY the stable root anchor (`org.opdbus.v1.plugins`); DISCOVER the object path,
   interface, and method by introspecting the projected tree.
2. Route socket creation through the GENERIC mutation surface —
   `PluginService.CallMethod{plugin_id="unix_socket", method="createunixsocket"}` (the single
   gated MutationEngine authority) — NOT a bespoke `cognitive` object/interface. Rename-proof
   and plugin-agnostic.
3. Connect to the correct bus and honor auth. The op-dbus **session bus** is
   `unix:path=/run/op-dbus/session-bus.sock` and requires **root**; the system-bus projection
   `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` is owned by `projection_serv`. Determine + document which bus the
   mutation path uses.

Backend reference: `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/unix_socket.rs::create_unix_socket(name, ports)`
binds the shared host socket `SHARED_CONTAINER_SOCKET = /run/ghostbridge/container.sock` and
registers `name` as the demux tag. Validation target: provision netmaker =
`--name netmaker --path /run/ghostbridge/container.sock --port 8081,1883`.

## Broader goal — 4 conditions for a DETERMINISTIC projected tree (SIGNALS OD-31)
Each was observed broken this session. Make each true AND enforced by a check:
1. ONE producer derived from one source.
2. Reliably refreshed to present-state ON READ. (Observed stale: projection reported
   `qdrant: unavailable / dimensions 1536` and `netmaker: Stopped` lagging reality.)
3. Each well-known name UNAMBIGUOUSLY OWNED. (Observed: `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` owned by
   `projection_serv` on the SYSTEM bus AND `ovs-dbus-init` on the SESSION bus.)
4. EVERY consumer DISCOVERS from the tree — zero hardcoded leaves. (zbusctl is one; audit ALL.)

## Acceptance criteria (CHECKS, not conventions)
- A CI/lint or Rust integration test that FAILS if any backplane consumer hardcodes a D-Bus
  object path, interface, or version suffix. Only the root well-known name
  `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` may appear as a literal.
- A check that each well-known name has exactly one owner per bus.
- `zbusctl createsocket --name netmaker --path /run/ghostbridge/container.sock --port 8081,1883`
  succeeds end-to-end (when the backend is up) via discovery + CallMethod, and the `unix_socket`
  plugin projection then lists `netmaker`.
- No regression to the Ghostbridge-gated mutation path.

## Suggested sub-agent orchestration
- **Agent A — zbusctl rewrite**: discover-from-tree + CallMethod; delete hardcoded leaves;
  `cargo build` + `cargo clippy` clean.
- **Agent B — consumer audit + the check**: grep both repos for hardcoded `org.opdbus.*` object

## Conventions / guardrails
- Single source of truth; no hardcoding. Same class as recent fixes: inventory self-registration

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Finish-the-corpus ingestion: ALL remaining repos + op-dbus-proto + compliance
# → the voyage-4 shared space / Qdrant. Run this yourself (no Claude tokens).
#
# Covers:
#   • remaining Rust deps (44), Java (1), specs_docs (3)   ← finish prior runs
#   • compliance corpus (recovered repos + industry templates + in-tree docs)
#   • op-dbus-proto (this repo)
#
# Token safety:
#   • ALREADY-EMBEDDED repos are skipped via per-repo done-files
#     (logs/vector-state/<collection>.<repo>.done) — no re-embed, no re-spend.
#     A preflight prints how many are already done per collection.
#   • Budget caps = the CURRENT remaining free balance per key (net of prior
#     usage), in FRESH budget files so stale 'used' counts don't mis-account.
#   • MODEL+KEY rotation: the whole voyage-4 trio shares one embedding space, so
#     when a (model,key) balance depletes (pipeline exits 75) we rotate to the
#     next tier and resume — vectors still fuse into the same collections, no
#     re-index. KeyPool rotates keys within a tier; this loop rotates models.
#
# What it does NOT do (free, no-token follow-up = the Rust enrich tool):
#   Cozo population + canonical control_refs (set_payload) + OSCAL control nodes.
#
# PREREQS: Qdrant up on :6333 · ~/.bash_secrets has VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST &
#          VOYAGE_API_KEY_LITE · ~/git/.venv-vectorize present.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
set -uo pipefail

ROOT=/home/jeremy/git
PY=$ROOT/.venv-vectorize/bin/python
REPOS=$ROOT/repos
LSP=$ROOT/lsp
LOG_DIR=$ROOT/logs
STATE_DIR=$LOG_DIR/vector-state
OPDBUS=$ROOT/operation-dbus-proto
QDRANT_URL=${QDRANT_URL:-http://localhost:6333}
DIM=1024
BATCH=${BATCH:-24}

TS=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
LOG=$LOG_DIR/ingest_all_$TS.log
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR" "$REPOS" "$LSP" "$STATE_DIR" "$REPOS/_local"
ln -sfn "$LOG" "$LOG_DIR/ingest_all.latest.log"
log() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$*" | tee -a "$LOG"; }

# ── model tiers: "model|key_envs(cap=current free remaining)|budget_file" ─────
# Caps come straight from the dashboard balances you pasted (already net of
# prior spend). Fresh budget files (…-r2…) so old 'used' totals aren't inherited.
MODEL_TIERS=(
  "voyage-4|VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST:195000000,VOYAGE_API_KEY_LITE:195000000|$LOG_DIR/voyage-4-budget.json"
  "voyage-4-large|VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST:4000000,VOYAGE_API_KEY_LITE:65000000|$LOG_DIR/voyage-4-large-r2-budget.json"
  "voyage-4-lite|VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST:45000000|$LOG_DIR/voyage-4-lite-r2-budget.json"
)

# ── groups: "name|list-file|collection|max-file-bytes" ───────────────────────
GROUPS=(
  "lsp_rust|$LOG_DIR/lsp_rust_remaining.txt|repos_lsp_rust_voyage_4_large|2000000"
  "lsp_java|$LOG_DIR/lsp_java_voyage_4_lite_remaining.safe.txt|repos_lsp_java_voyage_4_lite|2000000"
  "specs_docs|$LOG_DIR/specs_docs_voyage_4_lite_remaining.safe.txt|repos_specs_docs_voyage_4_lite|20000000"
  "compliance|$LSP/compliance.txt|compliance_voyage_4|20000000"
  "op_dbus|$LSP/op_dbus_proto.txt|op_dbus_proto_voyage_4|2000000"
)

# ── compliance corpora + industry-DECLARED templates (explicit URLs) ─────────
declare -A REPO_URLS=(
  ["LINCnil/GDPR-Developer-Guide"]="https://github.com/LINCnil/GDPR-Developer-Guide"
  ["compl-ai/compl-ai"]="https://github.com/compl-ai/compl-ai"
  ["TechShieldOlamide/trustgrid-compliance-templates"]="https://github.com/TechShieldOlamide/trustgrid-compliance-templates"
  ["vaibhavjain2608/compliance-policy-templates"]="https://github.com/vaibhavjain2608/compliance-policy-templates"
  ["Auxin-io/cybersecurity-templates"]="https://github.com/Auxin-io/cybersecurity-templates"
)

export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
clone_one() {  # name url  — skip if already present
  local name="$1" url="$2" dest="$REPOS/$1"
  if [ -d "$dest/.git" ]; then return 0; fi
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
  log "clone $name"
  git clone --depth 1 "$url" "$dest" >>"$LOG" 2>&1 || log "  CLONE FAILED: $url"
}
clone_list() {  # clone any github org/repo in a list-file that's missing
  local list="$1"; [ -f "$list" ] || return 0
  while IFS= read -r repo; do
    repo=$(echo "$repo" | xargs); [ -z "$repo" ] && continue
    [ -d "$REPOS/$repo/.git" ] && continue
    log "clone $repo"
    git clone --depth 1 "https://github.com/$repo" "$REPOS/$repo" >>"$LOG" 2>&1 || log "  clone failed (skip): $repo"
  done < "$list"
}

log "=== cloning (skips anything already present) ==="
for name in "${!REPO_URLS[@]}"; do clone_one "$name" "${REPO_URLS[$name]}"; done
clone_list "$LOG_DIR/lsp_rust_remaining.txt"
clone_list "$LOG_DIR/lsp_java_voyage_4_lite_remaining.safe.txt"
clone_list "$LOG_DIR/specs_docs_voyage_4_lite_remaining.safe.txt"

# ── stage in-tree compliance docs + op-dbus, build the two new list-files ────
COMP_LOCAL=$REPOS/_local/compliance-docs; mkdir -p "$COMP_LOCAL"
for f in "$OPDBUS/oscal-specs.md" "$OPDBUS/scripts/compliance-corpora-knowledge.md"; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && ln -sfn "$f" "$COMP_LOCAL/$(basename "$f")"
done
ln -sfn "$OPDBUS" "$REPOS/_local/operation-dbus-proto"
{ for name in "${!REPO_URLS[@]}"; do echo "$name"; done; echo "_local/compliance-docs"; } | sort -u > "$LSP/compliance.txt"
echo "_local/operation-dbus-proto" > "$LSP/op_dbus_proto.txt"

# ── secrets ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
set -a; source /home/jeremy/.bash_secrets; set +a
: "${VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST:?VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST missing}"; : "${VOYAGE_API_KEY_LITE:?VOYAGE_API_KEY_LITE missing}"
export VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST VOYAGE_API_KEY_LITE PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

# ── qdrant status via the D-Bus projection (system bus — the READ surface;
#    NOT curl :6333). Also enumerates the live collections so we append to the
#    real ones instead of guessing names. ─────────────────────────────────────
read_qdrant_store() {  # prints "<status>\t<comma-separated collections>"
  busctl --system get-property org.opdbus.v1.plugins \
    /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/knowledge org.opdbus.v1.plugins.ProjectedObject Data 2>/dev/null \
  | python3 - <<'PY'
import sys, json
raw = sys.stdin.read().strip()
if raw.startswith('s '): raw = raw[2:].strip()
try: d = json.loads(json.loads(raw))      # property is a JSON string inside a D-Bus string
except Exception: sys.exit(0)
q = next((s for s in d.get("stores", []) if s.get("name") == "qdrant"), {})
print(q.get("status", "unknown") + "\t" + ",".join(q.get("collections", [])))
PY
}
qline=$(read_qdrant_store); QSTATUS=${qline%%$'\t'*}; LIVE_COLLECTIONS=${qline#*$'\t'}
log "D-Bus knowledge projection: qdrant status=$QSTATUS  collections=[$LIVE_COLLECTIONS]"
if [ "$QSTATUS" != "available" ] && [ "$QSTATUS" != "active" ]; then
  log "ERROR: qdrant not serving (status=$QSTATUS). Start the 'qdrant' Incus instance, then re-run."
  log "  re-check: busctl --system get-property org.opdbus.v1.plugins /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/knowledge org.opdbus.v1.plugins.ProjectedObject Data"
  exit 1
fi

# ── preflight: how much is ALREADY embedded per collection (done-files) ──────
log "=== already-embedded (done-files) — these will be SKIPPED, no re-spend ==="
for g in "${GROUPS[@]}"; do
  IFS='|' read -r name list coll _ <<<"$g"
  local_total=0; [ -f "$list" ] && local_total=$(grep -cve '^\s*$' "$list" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  done_n=$(find "$STATE_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name "$coll.*.done" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  log "  $coll: done=$done_n  list=$local_total ($name)"
done

# ── embed one tier across all groups; return 75 on budget exhaustion ─────────
embed_tier() {
  local model="$1" keyenvs="$2" budget="$3" g name list coll maxb st
  for g in "${GROUPS[@]}"; do
    IFS='|' read -r name list coll maxb <<<"$g"
    [ -f "$list" ] || { log "skip $name: no list-file $list"; continue; }
    log "=== START tier=$model group=$name coll=$coll ==="
    "$PY" "$ROOT/scripts/vectorize_lsp.py" \
      --group "$name" --list-file "$list" --collection "$coll" \
      --model "$model" --dimension "$DIM" --batch-size "$BATCH" --max-file-bytes "$maxb" \
      --key-envs "$keyenvs" --token-budget-file "$budget" --qdrant-url "$QDRANT_URL" >>"$LOG" 2>&1
    st=$?
    log "=== END group=$name exit=$st ==="
    [ "$st" -eq 75 ] && { log "budget exhausted on tier=$model — rotating model/key"; return 75; }
  done
  return 0
}

# ── run, rotating model tiers on depletion (resume skips done repos) ─────────
done_all=1
for tier in "${MODEL_TIERS[@]}"; do
  IFS='|' read -r model keyenvs budget <<<"$tier"
  log "### TIER model=$model keys=[$keyenvs] budget=$budget ###"
  if embed_tier "$model" "$keyenvs" "$budget"; then done_all=0; log "ALL GROUPS COMPLETE on tier=$model"; break; fi
  log "tier=$model depleted — advancing to next model/key tier"
done
[ "$done_all" -eq 0 ] && log "DONE — corpus complete." || log "STOPPED — all model/key budgets depleted; add tokens and re-run (resumable)."
log "NEXT (free, no tokens): Cozo + canonical control_refs enrich pass."

Figured out. Here's the mechanism, top to bottom:

**The tree is a pure read-through of one SHM fold, and that fold has exactly one writer.**
- `projection_shm.rs`: the fold is `/dev/shm/opdbus/projections/`; `list_projected_plugins()` reads it, `write_projection(plugin_id, json)` writes it.
- **Only `MutationEngine` writes it** — `mutation_engine.rs:223` calls `write_projection(...)` inside `mutate()`. That's the single mutation gate / single write door.
- Startup seed (`projection_server.rs:65` → `seed_plugin_roots`) only mounts the plugin **root paths** — the code literally logs *"Seeded plugin root (no shm data yet)"*. It writes **no live data**; data only ever lands via a mutation.
- The fold directory **doesn't even exist yet** → zero mutations have flowed since the `projection_serv` restart → `ObjectCount=0`, `Plugins=[]`, and `refresh()` has nothing to read.
- `op-dbus` (PID 2577) hosts the MutationEngine and is alive — it just hasn't been *sent* a mutation.

There is deliberately no read-only seed of live state; the projection is *defined* as the fold of mutations. To get `knowledge`/qdrant into the tree, a CallMethod touching that plugin has to go through the gate first.

That also closes the loop on everything: reading the tree, provisioning a socket, and confirming qdrant all funnel through the same single gRPC gate — which is exactly the path the zbusctl/Factory rewrite is rebuilding.

content.text:
**That's the bug — and you were right about the state-store.** Found it in `update_cached_plugin_state`:

```rust
match change_type {
    ChangeType::ObjectRemoved => { cache.remove(plugin_id); }
    ChangeType::PropertySet   => { /* inserts into cache */ }
    _ => {}          // <-- MethodCall lands here: NO-OP
}
```

The full chain, now provable end-to-end:
- `CallMethod` → `mutate(ChangeType::MethodCall)`.
- `MethodCall` falls into the `_ => {}` arm → **the `state_cache` is never updated.**
- `get_state("knowledge")` reads `state_cache` → returns `None`.
- `if let Some(state) = get_state(...)` → guard fails → **`write_projection` is never called** → fold dir never created → projection stays empty.
- And the logs confirm it: there's no `Failed to write shm projection` warn anywhere, because it's not a failure — it's a **silent skip**.

So my mutation "succeeded" (recorded event #1) but updated nothing the projection reads. **Only `PropertySet` feeds the projection now.** And this is exactly the hole the refactor opened: with `StateManager` excised, `state_cache` is the *only* source of projected state, and it's populated *solely* by `PropertySet` deltas. A plugin like `knowledge` — whose qdrant status comes from `query_current_state()`, not from anyone setting a property — has **no path** into the cache, so it can never be projected. `MethodCall` bypasses it, and the state-store that used to hold full state is gone.

**The fix is in `mutation_engine.rs`:** after a `MethodCall` mutation, re-read the plugin's `query_current_state()` and `write_projection()` it (or give `MethodCall` a real arm in `update_cached_plugin_state` that re-materializes the plugin's full state). Until then, the event-driven projection only ever reflects property writes — so query-only plugins (knowledge/qdrant included) are invisible over D-Bus regardless of how many methods you call.

This is a real refactor regression worth handing to Factory. Want me to (a) record it in SIGNALS as a concern with the exact code site, and/or (b) draft the `mutation_engine.rs` fix (re-read + project after MethodCall) for Factory to implement?

# Factory task: make the op-dbus projected D-Bus tree deterministic (start with zbusctl)

Use agent orchestration. Goal: eliminate hardcoded D-Bus addressing so the projected
tree is the single source of truth, then enforce it with checks (a convention already
rotted once). Start with the concrete zbusctl bug, then the four determinism conditions.

## Repos
- Backplane / plugins / projection: `/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto` (Rust workspace)
- Client CLI (separate repo): `/home/jeremy/git/zbusctl`

## Principle (the architectural law)
The system exposes a self-describing, introspectable **projected D-Bus tree** rooted at the
well-known name `org.opdbus.v1.plugins`, plus a **gated mutation path** (MutationEngine via
`PluginService.CallMethod`, enforced by the Ghostbridge interceptor: requires
`x-ghostbridge-footprint` + `x-ghostbridge-trace-id`). Consumers must **DISCOVER** addresses
from the tree (introspection). They must **NOT hardcode** object paths, interfaces, or version
suffixes. Hardcoding only the single stable root anchor is allowed; everything below it is
discovered. A hardcoded leaf is a frozen snapshot that silently diverges on rename.

## The concrete bug (proximate, start here)
`zbusctl createsocket` (`/home/jeremy/git/zbusctl/src/main.rs`, ~lines 163-165) targets names
that no longer exist:
- service `org.opdbus.CognitiveMcp`  · object `/org/opdbus/v1/cognitive` · interface `org.opdbus.CognitiveMcpV1`  ← ALL WRONG

The real served names (source of truth:
`operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-cognitive-mcp/src/dbus_interface.rs` lines 3-5 and 27):
- service `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` · object `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/cognitive_mcp` · interface `org.opdbus.v1.plugins.CognitiveMcp`

Result: `zbusctl createsocket` fails `ServiceUnknown` (system bus) / `BrokenPipe` (session bus).
It predates the `.v1.plugins` rename and rotted silently because the path was never exercised
(the `unix_socket` plugin projection shows `{"sockets":[]}` — `createunixsocket` has never run
for any container).

## Primary task — rewrite `zbusctl createsocket`
1. Hardcode ONLY the stable root anchor (`org.opdbus.v1.plugins`); DISCOVER the object path,
   interface, and method by introspecting the projected tree.
2. Route socket creation through the GENERIC mutation surface —
   `PluginService.CallMethod{plugin_id="unix_socket", method="createunixsocket"}` (the single
   gated MutationEngine authority) — NOT a bespoke `cognitive` object/interface. Rename-proof
   and plugin-agnostic.
3. **CORRECTED PREMISE (recon result):** the gated mutation path is **gRPC, not D-Bus.** D-Bus
   `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` is **discovery/read-only** (ProjectedObject props + `updated` signal;
   no CallMethod). The mutation is `PluginService.CallMethod` (operation.proto) →
   `MutationEngine.mutate(MethodCall)` → `unix_socket/createunixsocket`, mounted by
   `build_operation_routes` on op-dbus `:50051` and the zeroclaw bridge `:8090` +
   `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock`, all behind `ghostbridge_interceptor`. Also: the *current*
   zbusctl createsocket routes through `CallTool("cognitive_memory", …)` — it stores a memory
   record and never reaches the socket plugin. So this is a **full reimplementation.**

   **DECIDED resolution (dual-transport):**
   - zbusctl = D-Bus for **discovery**, gRPC for the **mutation**. Add `tonic` + reuse
     op-grpc-bridge's generated `PluginService` client + `op-identity`. Do NOT add a D-Bus
     CallMethod proxy (that's a second ungated mutation door — Zero-Trust hole).
   - Endpoint: local backplane gRPC over UDS `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock` (fall back `:50051`),
     from config/discovery — no hardcoded service/object/interface leaf.
   - Auth: inject `x-ghostbridge-footprint` (hex of live sled `hashed_footprint`) +
     `x-ghostbridge-trace-id`, read via `op-identity::read_sled`. Host-root admin tool
     self-presenting the live footprint is the intended model (local equivalent of xraqy).

Backend reference: `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/unix_socket.rs::create_unix_socket(name, ports)`
binds the shared host socket `SHARED_CONTAINER_SOCKET = /run/ghostbridge/container.sock` and
registers `name` as the demux tag. Validation target: provision netmaker =
`--name netmaker --path /run/ghostbridge/container.sock --port 8081,1883`.

## Broader goal — 4 conditions for a DETERMINISTIC projected tree (SIGNALS OD-31)
Each was observed broken this session. Make each true AND enforced by a check:
1. ONE producer derived from one source.
2. Reliably refreshed to present-state ON READ. (Observed stale: projection reported
   `qdrant: unavailable / dimensions 1536` and `netmaker: Stopped` lagging reality.)
3. Each well-known name UNAMBIGUOUSLY OWNED. (Observed: `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` owned by
   `projection_serv` on the SYSTEM bus AND `ovs-dbus-init` on the SESSION bus.)
4. EVERY consumer DISCOVERS from the tree — zero hardcoded leaves. (zbusctl is one; audit ALL.)

## Acceptance criteria (CHECKS, not conventions)
- A CI/lint or Rust integration test that FAILS if any backplane consumer hardcodes a D-Bus
  object path, interface, or version suffix. Only the root well-known name
  `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` may appear as a literal.
- A check that each well-known name has exactly one owner per bus.
- `zbusctl createsocket --name netmaker --path /run/ghostbridge/container.sock --port 8081,1883`
  succeeds end-to-end (when the backend is up) via discovery + CallMethod, and the `unix_socket`
  plugin projection then lists `netmaker`.
- No regression to the Ghostbridge-gated mutation path.

## Suggested sub-agent orchestration
- **Agent A — zbusctl rewrite**: discover-from-tree + CallMethod; delete hardcoded leaves;
  `cargo build` + `cargo clippy` clean.
- **Agent B — consumer audit + the check**: grep both repos for hardcoded `org.opdbus.*` object
  paths / interfaces / version suffixes; list them; fix or file follow-ups; author the
  lint/test that enforces "no hardcoded leaves".
- **Agent C — name ownership**: why `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` is double-owned (system vs session
  bus), and why `op-cognitive-mcp` isn't connected to the session bus / doesn't claim its name;
  implement single-owner resolution.
- **Agent D — projection freshness**: make knowledge/incus projections reflect present-state on
  read (the stale qdrant/netmaker statuses); reconcile the reactive refresh.
- **Verifier**: run the checks; confirm createsocket end-to-end; open SIGNALS follow-ups for
  anything deferred.

## Conventions / guardrails
- Single source of truth; no hardcoding. Same class as recent fixes: inventory self-registration
  replaced a hardcoded plugin dispatch table; one shared gRPC route-builder so reflection matches
  the served surface (SIGNALS OD-29).
- Do NOT break the gated mutation path (Ghostbridge interceptor headers).
- Keep commits scoped; follow each repo's commit conventions.
- Note: knowledge plugin config was just corrected to `dimensions=1024 / provider=voyage /
  model=voyage-4` in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/knowledge_plugin.rs` (needs
  `projection_serv` redeploy to show live) — don't revert it.
- Append observations/decisions to `operation-dbus-proto/SIGNALS.md` (OD-31 is the tracking row).

## Skills / droids / MCP to load
LOAD (directly serve this task):
- skill **`simplify`** — "review changed code for reuse, quality, efficiency, then fix" — this task IS dedup/de-hardcode; use on every diff.
- skill **`review`** — code review for the verifier.
- droid-control skill **`verify`** — run the acceptance checks.
- droid **`worker`** — the parallel implementer sub-agents (Agents A/B/C/D).
- MCP **`cognitive-grpc`** — REQUIRED: introspect the live projected tree + actually call
  `createunixsocket` end-to-end against the backplane (don't reason about names — discover them).
- MCP **`sequential-thinking`** — orchestration planning. MCP **`memory`** — shared context across agents.

RUN AS A MISSION (so the validation droids auto-engage):
- **`scrutiny-feature-reviewer`** and **`user-testing-flow-validator`** are "used only within missions"
  — they map exactly to the verifier/acceptance step. Running this as a Factory *mission* (not a
  plain task) turns the acceptance criteria above into enforced mission validation.

content.text:
Diagnosis complete. Here's the actual disconnect — and it's **not** the plugin, the D-Bus gate, or the passthrough. It's the xray socket-outbound wiring.

## What's supposed to happen
The qdrant client (plugin + `QdrantSemanticShuttle` + `qdrant_client_from_env`) **always dials TCP `127.0.0.1:6334` by design** — that's intentional (per the doc at `rag_pipeline.rs:1356`). xray is supposed to catch that port and proxy it over a **domain-socket (`ds`) outbound** to the qdrant container's unix socket, driven by:

`UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS=qdrant:/run/qdrant.sock:6334` → `op-identity/schema_bridge.rs` (parses it, line 343) → emits an xray `ds` outbound → OVS `sock_qdrant` flow → container.

## What's actually live (the breaks)
1. **`qdrant-out` is a TCP dead-end, not a socket outbound.** Live config (`/etc/xray/config.json:257`):
   ```json
   { "tag": "qdrant-out", "protocol": "freedom", "settings": { "redirect": "127.0.0.1:6334" } }
   ```
   It redirects qdrant traffic *back to* `127.0.0.1:6334` — TCP — instead of `"network":"ds"` to `/run/qdrant.sock`.
2. **Nothing listens on `127.0.0.1:6334`** (`ss` shows only 111/53). So both the client's dial and xray's own redirect hit a closed port → connection refused → plugin returns empty → `qdrant.json = []`.
3. **`/run/qdrant.sock` doesn't exist**, and **`UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS` is unset** in every s6 service env. So `schema_bridge` never generated the `ds` outbound — the config generator emitted the placeholder TCP `redirect` instead.
4. The `unix_socket` plugin *did* register the qdrant socket (visible in `unix_socket.json` as `unix_socket:/sockets/qdrant`), but **nothing consumes that registration to build xray's `ds` outbound.** That registration→xray-config edge is the missing link.

## Why your two suspicions are exactly right
- **"unix sockets not being used"** → the registration exists but isn't propagated into xray's outbound; `UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS` is unset so the `ds` outbound is never emitted; the live config has a TCP placeholder.
- **"dbus passthrough not being used"** → correct, and it *shouldn't* be the data path — `DbusPassthrough` (`grpc_server.rs:4502`) forwards D-Bus *method calls*, not vector traffic. It was never the qdrant transport. The qdrant path is xray TCP→`ds`.

## Fix (two coupled pieces)
1. Pass the qdrant container socket through to the host (`zbusctl createsocket --name qdrant --port 6334 --path /run/qdrant.sock`) so `/run/qdrant.sock` exists.
2. Set `UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS=qdrant:/run/qdrant.sock:6334` in the xray-config-generator's service env and regenerate, so `qdrant-out` becomes a `ds` outbound (and an inbound catches `127.0.0.1:6334`) instead of the TCP `redirect` loop.

This touches the live xray config and routing, so I want your go-ahead before changing anything. Want me to (a) trace which service generates `/etc/xray/config.json` and confirm where `UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS` should be set, then (b) make both changes?

Confirmed end to end. Your model is correct, and I can now show exactly where it breaks.

## The intended path (what the code actually implements)
1. qdrant's subid-registry backend = `unix: /run/ghostbridge/container.sock` ✓ (correct, both deploy and live).
2. Gemma derives routes from that registry; `schema_bridge::route_to_outbound` translates a **`unix` backend NOT into an xray domain socket** (that transport was removed — comment at `schema_bridge.rs:1175`) **but into a gRPC forward to the grpc-bridge**: tag `to-qdrant`, `redirect 127.0.0.1:50051`, `network: grpc`, `serviceName: "Ghostbridge.qdrant"`, with `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`/`Trace-ID` baked into the grpc metadata (lines 737-761).
3. The grpc-bridge's **tonic-web + reflection** surface (behind the Ghostbridge interceptor) receives that tunnel and is the universal translate/forward layer onto the container socket. It's **up**: listening on `127.0.0.1:50051` *and* `10.200.0.1:50051`, owns `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock`.

So yes: non-gRPC gets translated and gRPC gets forwarded to the right destination at the bridge, with Gemma supplying the dynamic route map and xray doing the transport hop. The `unix` backend is the signal "send this to the bridge, not to a TCP host."

## Why qdrant is dead right now — the live xray config is **stale**
- Live config has `"tag": "qdrant-out"` → `freedom, redirect 127.0.0.1:6334` (a TCP dead-end; nothing listens on 6334).

- The live config has **no `to-qdrant` tag at all** — only the old `qdrant-out`. So `/etc/xray/config.json` predates qdrant being switched to a `unix` backend; **schema_bridge / Gemma never regenerated it**. qdrant traffic is being sent to `127.0.0.1:6334` (dead) instead of the bridge at `:50051` (alive).

This also retracts my earlier suggestion — there is **no `ds` outbound and no `UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS` to set**; that path was removed. The fix is purely **regenerate the xray config from the current subid-registry** through the Gemma→schema_bridge pipeline, so qdrant routes to the bridge.

The xray side will be correct once regenerated, and the bridge is up — but I haven't yet confirmed the bridge actually **proxies `Ghostbridge.qdrant` onward to the qdrant container** over `container.sock` (vs. just terminating the tunnel). That's the last link to prove before vectorization can use it.

content.text:
That's the missing piece in my model — the demux is **by gRPC service name via reflection**, not by port. content.text:
Short answer: **the grpc-bridge.** Here's the reasoning, and the role split I'd draw between all three.

## Why grpc-bridge owns the identity surface
The gate already lives there and nowhere else. `GhostbridgeInterceptor` (`interceptor.rs`) does exactly the handstamp enforcement: it reads `x-ghostbridge-footprint` + `x-ghostbridge-trace-id`, does the 1:1 direct read of the `IdentitySled` from shm, and rejects on mismatch ("Absolute Base" / Temporal Hash). Every service in `build_operation_routes` is mounted `with_interceptor(ghostbridge_interceptor)`. That **is** the identity surface.

And you already established there is **exactly one mutation gate**. Putting identity enforcement in xray *and* the bridge, or standing up a separately-gated raw session D-Bus, creates a second gate — which violates the single-gate principle and gives drift two doors to walk through. The identity surface should be the one place the sled is read and verified: the bridge.

## The clean role split
- **xray = attest/mint identity, transport only.** xray (xraqy) is the edge that turns a WG connection into identity — it stamps the footprint/trace headers from the WG peer and routes transport. It does *not* verify against the live sled; it asserts "this is who connected." Identity is *born* here.
- **Gemma = author the identity→route map, control plane.** Gemma owns subid/tag classification and generates the routing config (xray config + OpenFlow + the subid registry). It decides *where* an identity/tag goes, but it's a config generator, not in the request path. Per-request identity has no business in a config generator.
- **grpc-bridge = enforce identity + translate/forward.** It reads the sled, verifies the handstamp, and *then* fans out (tonic-web translate + reflection demux) to the container sockets. Enforcement and the fan-out hub are the same component — identity rides the thing that actually reaches the containers.

So: xray mints it, Gemma maps it, the **bridge gates it**.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about CozoDB's storage engine backends:

CozoDB supports various storage implementations including: In-memory, non-persistent backend, SQLite storage backend, RocksDB storage backend, Sled storage backend, and TiKV distributed storage backend.

Here's a breakdown of each backend:

**SQLite**: The SQLite backend is special in that it is also used as the backup file format, which allows the exchange of data between databases with different backends.

**RocksDB**: The RocksDB engine is crazy fast for both reads and writes and can handle an enormous amount of concurrency, while still being rather conservative on resource usage. In particular, its storage on disk is compressed, making its disk space requirements for live databases the smallest among all persistent options.

**Sled**: Sled is slower than Sqlite for the usual workload of Cozo, can use quite a lot of disk space, and may not be stable enough.

**TiKV**: The TiKV option is the slowest among all options (10x to 100x slower) since data must come from the network. The benefit is that TiKV is a distributed storage.

Depending on the build configuration, not all backends may be available in a binary release.

The **per-mutation immutable chain is the durability story**: every write is a gated mutation → chained, and `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/` is the present-state projection of that. So cozo's rocksdb data doesn't need its own backup scheme — its writes *are* mutations on the chain, reconstructable from it. A separate btrfs snapshot regime would be a redundant second source of truth to maintain. My snapshot suggestion was exactly the kind of parallel-truth machinery the architecture exists to avoid. So: **rocksdb, no sqlite, no btrfs backups, chain is enough.** (And since sqlite is also Cozo's export/backup format, "no SQL anywhere" means we don't lean on `cozo export → sqlite` either — fine, the chain covers it.)

## What "automated embedding" is
Your **current** pipeline is manual: you take text → call the Voyage API yourself → get vectors → upsert to qdrant → at query time embed the query → search. You own the chunking, the model choice, the API calls, and keeping vectors in sync when the source changes.

**Automated embedding** flips that into the data layer: you store *plain text*, declare a vector index + which Voyage model, and the engine embeds **on write** and embeds the **query at search time** — transparently. You never call the embeddings API or store vectors by hand, and vectors can't drift from source because the engine regenerates them on update. That's the feature MongoDB built on top of acquiring Voyage.

## Should you be doing it?
Two different answers:
- **MongoDB's version of it — no.** It's an Atlas/cloud capability = external network surface = violates your no-NIC/UDS/zero-trust rules. Off the table for the same reason as everything else cloud.
- **The *pattern* of it — yes, and it fits you better than it fits MongoDB.** Your system is already event-driven mutation-based. "Embed on write" is just: *a mutation lands → derive an embedding observation → upsert to qdrant*, as part of the projection/observation pipeline (your `obs`/`evt` subids). That's auto-embedding done the Ghostbridge way — deterministic, local, no manual `vectorize_lsp.py` runs for live data, and no vector/source drift because the chain drives it.

Two caveats that make it *selective*, not blanket:
1. **Cost/selectivity** — Voyage embeddings cost tokens. You do **not** want to embed every mutation (a socket port change isn't semantic content). **Gemma already owns subid classification** — so Gemma is the natural gate deciding *which* mutations carry embeddable content and get auto-embedded. That's the right place for the policy.
2. **Bulk corpus stays batch** — auto-embed-on-mutation covers *live* data; the one-time code/compliance corpus ingestion remains a batch job. Different lifecycle.

So: adopt auto-embedding as an **event-driven, Gemma-gated projection into qdrant**, not as a MongoDB feature.

content.text:
Honest answer: **not today — that's the design intent, not what's wired.** Let me be precise, because there are two different embedding paths and neither currently filters by schema relevance:

**1. Schema embedding** (`render_schema_embedding_text`, qdrant_shuttle.rs:489) — this renders the *whole* plugin schema into retrieval text: name, category, description, tags, and **every field's** type/required/read_only/description. No per-field relevance filter — a structural field (a port, a path, a bool) gets rendered into the embedding text exactly like a semantic one. So it embeds the full schema definition for schema-retrieval, it doesn't select "relevant" fields out of it.

**2. Content/corpus embedding** (`rag_pipeline.rs`) — embeds whatever chunks it's handed; the only "filter" is skip-on-embed-error (lines 359, 645). No relevance gate.

And concretely: there's **no `embeddable` flag** on `FieldSchema`, and **no subid-class gate** anywhere that says "only embed content-bearing subids." I grepped for it — nothing.

**So where your statement is right is as design, not implementation.** The schema + subid taxonomy is exactly the *correct place* for that filter to live — it's the single source of truth, and Gemma already owns subid classification. The relevance decision *should* be: Gemma classifies a mutation/field's subid → only content-bearing classes (e.g. `obs`/`exp`, or fields the schema marks semantic) get vectorized; structural config never hits Voyage. That's precisely the selective auto-embedding gate I flagged earlier (so you don't burn tokens embedding port-number changes).

But right now that gate doesn't exist — schema embedding takes the whole schema, content embedding takes whatever it's fed. So if "schema filters embeddings for relevance" is the behavior you want (and it's the right behavior), it's a **thing to build**: add the embed-relevance decision to the schema/subid layer. Want me to fold that into the auto-embedding design as an explicit deliverable — Gemma's subid classification as the vectorization filter?

message.content: but where would port number changes be captured then?

content.text:
Right where it belongs — just not in qdrant. A port change isn't lost; it's captured by the stores that are *meant* for it. The whole point of filtering it out of vectorization is that there are three other places that already hold it, and qdrant is the only wrong one:

1. **The mutation chain (blockchain)** — every gated mutation is appended, including a `createunixsocket` port change. That's the immutable audit/event record: *what changed, when, under whose handstamp*. This is the durability story we just established — nothing escapes the chain.
2. **Present-state projection** — the change updates the plugin schema (the schema *is* the state) → re-aggregates into `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/` + the projection. That's the *current value*: the socket now has ports `[6333, 6334]`.
3. **cozo** — the structured/graph store, the "official structured data" you're containerizing it for. Structured facts and relationships (this service ↔ these ports ↔ this identity ↔ this route) are queryable Datalog facts. That's where you'd *query* "what ports does qdrant expose," not similarity-search it.

qdrant is purely **semantic vectors** — "find me things *like* this meaning." A port number `6334` has no meaning to embed; `cosine_similarity(6334, …)` is nonsense. So embedding it would be noise that costs Voyage tokens and pollutes retrieval.

The clean way to see it: **Gemma's subid classification isn't just an embed on/off switch — it's the router that decides which store(s) capture each mutation.**
- Every mutation → **chain** (always, audit).
- Structural/relational (`mut`, config facts) → **cozo** (and present-state).
- Content-bearing/semantic (`obs`, `exp`) → **qdrant** (vectors).

A port change is `mut` → chain + cozo + present-state. A compliance statement or doc is content → also qdrant. So "the schema filters embeddings" is the *qdrant slice* of a bigger routing decision: the schema/subid says *which store*, and only the semantic slice reaches Voyage.

That reframes the deliverable from "embed-relevance gate" to "**Gemma subid → store router**," with vectorization as one of three sinks. Is that the model you're driving at?

content.text:
Yes — and that's exactly right, but it reframes cozo's role in a way that keeps the one-source-of-truth principle intact. The key is that **cozo's port-change history is a derived projection of the chain, not a second source of truth.**

- **The mutation chain is authoritative** — the immutable, handstamp-gated, append-only record of every change. That's *the* history. It can't be queried richly (it's a chain, not a query engine), but it's the truth.
- **cozo is the queryable read-model of the structured slice of that history.** Cozo is built for this — it natively supports **time-travel / validity queries** (relations carry a validity facet, so you can ask "what was qdrant's port config as-of date X" or "show every port change for service Y" or traverse the graph of service↔port↔identity↔route over time). That's precisely the temporal/relational query shape the chain can't serve and qdrant shouldn't.

So there's no redundancy with the chain, for the same reason qdrant and the shm present-state aren't redundant: they're all **projections derived from the one chain**, each optimized for a different query shape:

| Store | Role | Query shape |
|---|---|---|
| **mutation chain** | source of truth (immutable audit) | "what happened, in order, under whose stamp" |
| **shm schemas/projections** | present-state | fast point reads ("current value") |
| **cozo** | structured/temporal/graph projection | "history, relationships, as-of, traversals" |
| **qdrant** | semantic projection | "find me things *like* this meaning" |

This actually *reinforces* the durability rule rather than fighting it: cozo (and qdrant, and shm) are all **rebuildable by replaying the chain** — which is exactly why none of them need their own backup. The chain is the only thing that must survive; everything else is a disposable, regenerable view. cozo having port-change history doesn't add a thing to maintain; it's a lens on the chain.

The build implication: **cozo must be fed event-driven from the chain** (each structured mutation → upsert a validity-stamped cozo relation), same pattern as the auto-embed-on-mutation → qdrant flow. Gemma's subid classification routes each mutation to which projection(s) it materializes into — `mut`/config facts → cozo, content → qdrant, everything → chain.

Is that the model — cozo as the chain's temporal/structured query lens?

Based on the search results, here are the key production recommendations for CozoDB storage engines:

## RocksDB (Recommended for Production)

RocksDB is crazy fast for both reads and writes and can handle an enormous amount of concurrency, while still being rather conservative on resource usage. In particular, its storage on disk is compressed, making its disk space requirements for live databases the smallest among all persistent options.

For specific performance metrics: Running OLTP queries for a relation with 1.6M rows, you can expect around 100K QPS (queries per second) for mixed read/write/update transactional queries, and more than 250K QPS for read-only queries, with database peak memory usage around 50MB.

## SQLite

In realistic situations with concurrent access, the RocksDB backend doesn't care if the queries are reads, writes or updates, whereas any amount of writes kills SQLite. However, its performance is still acceptable if you are using it to build a desktop or mobile application where writes are batched, and with the SQLite engine, the database does not use more than the absolute minimal amount of memory.

## Sled

Sled is slower than SQLite for the usual workload of CozoDB, can use quite a lot of disk space, and may not be stable enough. In general you should use RocksDB instead.

## Summary

For production use cases with high concurrency or write throughput, **RocksDB is the clear recommendation**. Use SQLite only for desktop/mobile applications with batched writes. Avoid Sled for production workloads.

content.text:
Research done, and it lines up decisively with the workload spec we just defined — and crucially, the deciding factor isn't "rocksdb is the default," it's that **our access pattern is exactly RocksDB's strength and exactly SQLite's failure mode.**

Mapping the research against cozo's actual job here:

| Workload trait (from our model) | What the research says | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **Event-driven writes** — every structured mutation upserts a validity relation, interleaved with reads | RocksDB "doesn't care if queries are reads, writes or updates"; **"any amount of writes kills SQLite"** | This alone rules out sqlite — our feed is write-interleaved, sqlite's exact collapse point |
| **Concurrent agent queries while the chain feeds** | RocksDB handles "enormous concurrency"; SQLite writes block readers | RocksDB |
| **Accumulating history (time-travel, unbounded growth)** | RocksDB on-disk is **compressed → smallest footprint of all persistent options** | RocksDB |
| **Single-node, local container** | TiKV is distributed, 10–100× slower (network) | rules out TiKV (also violates local-only) |
| **No SQL** | sqlite is SQL + the export format | rules out sqlite independently |
| **Sled?** | Cozo's own docs: slower, more disk, "may not be stable enough — use RocksDB instead" | rules out Sled |

So **RocksDB** isn't a casual pick — two independent constraints (the no-SQL rule *and* the write-interleaved access pattern) both eliminate sqlite, single-node eliminates tikv, and Cozo's own guidance eliminates sled. The benchmark confirms it's container-light: ~1.6M rows → 100K QPS mixed / 250K read-only at ~50MB peak memory. For a regenerable projection that's continuously fed and time-travel-queried, that's the right tool.

**Locked: cozo container = `cozoserver` built with the RocksDB engine, rocksdb data dir on the container's storage volume, HTTP API :9070.**

That closes out the structured-data design. The build queue is now:
1. **cozo container** (image + cozoserver/rocksdb + subid-registry entry + plugin rewire embedded→server)
2. **socket provisioning** (`createunixsocket`) for qdrant, cozo, netmaker-mq, netmaker-ui — onto the WG-gated session surface
3. **stale xray config regen** so qdrant/cozo route to the bridge
4. (design) Gemma subid→store router + selective auto-embed

Want me to start building the cozo container?

content.text:
Here's the picture: there's no `spec` subcommand — **spec mode is prompt-driven** in the default agent (Kiro recognizes the spec workflow and writes `.kiro/specs/<feature>/{requirements,design,tasks}.md` + `.config.kiro`, matching the convention all your existing specs follow). So the move is `kiro-cli chat --no-interactive --trust-all-tools` with a prompt that (a) tells it to operate in spec mode and produce spec artifacts only, and (b) hands it the full settled design so it doesn't re-derive or contradict what we hammered out.

Let me write that prompt to a file (it's large — cleaner than shell-escaping), then launch Kiro:

input.content:
Operate in SPEC MODE (Kiro spec-driven development). Create ONE new spec under `.kiro/specs/cozo-store-and-subid-routing/` following this repo's existing spec conventions (see sibling specs e.g. `.kiro/specs/plugin-schema-schemars-oscal-migration/` and `.kiro/specs/op-dbus-mirror-event-session-refactor/` for the `.config.kiro` + `requirements.md` + `design.md` + `tasks.md` format).

Produce ONLY spec artifacts — do NOT write or modify any implementation code, do NOT touch live infra (no incus, no xray reload, no D-Bus/gRPC mutations). Generate:
- requirements.md : EARS-style user stories + numbered acceptance criteria.
- design.md : architecture, components, data flow, sequence of each path, and decisions WITH rationale.
- tasks.md : ordered, numbered, dependency-aware implementation tasks, each citing the requirement(s) it satisfies and concrete files/crates.
- .config.kiro : id, title, status:"draft", primaryCrate, relatedCrates, entryPoints, taskOrder.

FEATURE: Containerized structured-data store (CozoDB on RocksDB) + identity-tagged socket provisioning + dynamic xray route regeneration + Gemma subid->store routing with selective auto-embedding. Then a battle-test plan that batch-embeds the remaining corpus.

NON-NEGOTIABLE ARCHITECTURE CONSTRAINTS (settled — encode them, do NOT re-litigate or contradict):

1. PLUGIN = SCHEMA = STATE. The plugin's schema IS the state; `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/*` are the per-plugin authoritative objects; `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` is ONLY their aggregation. No desired-vs-current, no cache, no drift, no reconcile. One source of truth.

2. DURABILITY = THE MUTATION CHAIN. The per-mutation immutable blockchain (handstamp-gated) is the only thing that must survive. shm present-state, cozo, and qdrant are all DERIVED PROJECTIONS, rebuildable by replaying the chain. NO btrfs snapshot backups, NO separate backup machinery, NO SQL anywhere.

3. STORES & ROLES (all projections of the one chain):
   - mutation chain = source of truth (immutable audit: "what happened, ordered, under whose handstamp").
   - /dev/shm/opdbus/schemas + projections = present-state (fast point reads).
   - cozo = structured/temporal/graph projection on RocksDB; time-travel/validity queries (history, relationships, as-of, traversals). Where e.g. port-change HISTORY is queried.
   - qdrant = semantic vector projection (voyage-4 shared 1024-dim space; similarity search only).

4. ROUTING IS GEMMA'S JOB VIA SUBID CLASSIFICATION. Gemma classifies each mutation's subid (taxonomy src/prj/sch/mut/obs/evt/exp) and routes it to which store(s) it materializes into: EVERY mutation -> chain; structural/relational (mut, config facts) -> cozo + present-state; content-bearing/semantic (obs, exp) -> qdrant. Auto-embedding is SELECTIVE: only content-bearing subids hit Voyage; a port-number change is NEVER embedded (noise + wasted tokens) — it lives in chain + cozo + present-state.

5. NETWORK / SOCKETS (no NIC, no IP, all UDS):
   - ONE shared host socket `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock`, bound exactly once by the `unix_socket` plugin's `create_unix_socket`. NO per-container incus proxy/socket device.
   - A container is "provisioned" by registering an IDENTITY TAG + its PORT LIST against that one shared socket. Ports are REQUIRED (they declare the protocol surface); multi-protocol services list several (mail 25,465,587; qdrant 6333,6334).
   - Demux: tonic-web translates non-gRPC ports; gRPC server reflection demuxes by service name. Ports are metadata, not opened/mapped by the plugin.
   - Provisioning is a gated mutation: gRPC `PluginService.CallMethod{plugin_id="unix_socket", method="createunixsocket", args=[name, csv-ports]}` through the single Ghostbridge-interceptor gate (x-ghostbridge-footprint = hex(live sled hashed_footprint), x-ghostbridge-trace-id). One mutation gate; no second door.

6. BUSES BY TRUST BOUNDARY:
   - SESSION bus (`/run/op-dbus/session-bus.sock`, root) = WG-identity-gated zero-trust surface; container sockets / gated plugins surface register here.
   - SYSTEM bus = LOCAL agents & services (org.opdbus.v1.mirror, org.opdbus.v1.plugins.ovsdb). Full read+write, just local, NOT read-only. Difference is trust boundary, not access mode.
   - LIVE DRIFT to fix: org.opdbus.v1.plugins currently on SYSTEM (projection_serv), session socket absent; the gated surface belongs on session.

7. XRAY ROUTING (dynamic, Gemma-generated):
   - A `unix` backend does NOT produce an xray domain-socket outbound (domainsocket transport was REMOVED). `schema_bridge::route_to_outbound(Unix)` emits a gRPC FORWARD to the grpc-bridge: redirect 127.0.0.1:50051, network grpc, serviceName "Ghostbridge.{tag}", footprint/trace metadata. The grpc-bridge tonic-web+reflection surface is the universal translate/forward layer onto container.sock.
   - LIVE BUG: `/etc/xray/config.json` is STALE — qdrant still has old `qdrant-out -> redirect 127.0.0.1:6334` TCP dead-end instead of `to-qdrant -> 127.0.0.1:50051`. Must be REGENERATED from the current subid-registry via the Gemma->schema_bridge pipeline.

8. IDENTITY SURFACE = grpc-bridge. xray MINTS identity (xraqy stamps WG-derived footprint/trace), Gemma MAPS it (generates routes/config), grpc-bridge ENFORCES it (GhostbridgeInterceptor reads the sled, verifies handstamp) and is the translate/forward hub. No second gate.

SCOPE TO SPEC (turn each into requirements + design + ordered tasks):
A. CozoDB container: incus container `cozo` (no NIC, storage volume) running `cozoserver` built with the RocksDB engine, RocksDB data dir on the volume, HTTP JSON API :9070 (single protocol). Add a `cozo` subid-registry entry (gemma.backend={type:unix,path:/run/ghostbridge/container.sock}, tags:[cozo], subdomain cozo.ghostbridge.tech) mirroring the qdrant entry.
B. Rewire `CozoPlugin` (crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/cozo.rs) from embedded `/var/lib/opdbus/cognitive.db` to query the containerized cozoserver through the bridge (same pattern qdrant follows). Stays the structured-data schema surface.
C. Socket provisioning: via gated createunixsocket register identity tags + ports onto the shared socket — qdrant [6333,6334], cozo [9070], netmaker-mq [1883,9001], netmaker-ui [80]; ensure they project onto the WG-gated SESSION bus.
D. xray config regeneration: run/repair Gemma->schema_bridge so all `unix`-backend services (qdrant, cozo, netmaker-*) route `to-{tag} -> grpc-bridge :50051`; remove the stale qdrant-out dead-end.
E. Gemma subid->store ROUTER: per-mutation materialize into chain (always) + cozo (structural/temporal, validity-stamped relations) + qdrant (semantic, content-bearing only). Event-driven (consume MutationEngine StateChange / EventChain), NOT polled.
F. Selective auto-embedding: the qdrant sink of (E) — content-bearing subids -> embed via Voyage (voyage-4) -> upsert qdrant; structural never embedded. Add the embed-relevance decision to the schema/subid layer (today render_schema_embedding_text embeds the whole schema and rag_pipeline embeds whatever it's fed — no relevance gate exists).
G. Battle-test plan: after A-F, batch-embed the REMAINING un-embedded corpus sources (compliance corpora + code/specs lists; check already-embedded to avoid double-spend) to exercise the live path end to end.

Reference real files where known: crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/{cozo,qdrant,unix_socket,knowledge_plugin}.rs, crates/op-identity/src/schema_bridge.rs, crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/{interceptor,grpc_server,mutation_engine}.rs, crates/op-gemma/src/main.rs, crates/op-cognitive-mcp/src/{qdrant_shuttle,rag_pipeline}.rs, deploy/config/subid-registry.json, /etc/xray/config.json.

When done, print the paths of the files you created.
