1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Setup Qdrant in an Incus container with no NIC, exposed via a single
3	# Unix socket at /run/qdrant.sock (gRPC port 6334).
4	#
5	# Usage: sudo bash deploy/setup-qdrant-incus.sh
6	set -euo pipefail
7	
8	CONTAINER="qdrant"
9	QDRANT_VERSION="v1.18.1"
10	QDRANT_URL="https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/releases/download/${QDRANT_VERSION}/qdrant-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz"
11	STORAGE_POOL="default"
12	# Local gRPC port — xray proxies 127.0.0.1:$QDRANT_PORT → container via ds transport.
13	QDRANT_PORT=6334
14	
15	log() { echo "[qdrant-setup] $*"; }
16	die() { echo "[qdrant-setup] ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
17	
18	# ─── preflight ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
19	
20	[[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die "Run as root: sudo bash $0"
21	command -v incus &>/dev/null || die "incus not found"
22	
23	# Initialise Incus storage if this is a fresh system
24	if ! incus storage list --format csv 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
25	    log "Initialising Incus with default storage pool (dir backend)"
26	    incus admin init --preseed <<'PRESEED'
27	config: {}
28	networks: []
29	storage_pools:
30	- config: {}
31	  description: ""
32	  name: default
33	  driver: dir
34	profiles:
35	- config: {}
36	  description: ""
37	  devices:
38	    root:
39	      path: /
40	      pool: default
41	      type: disk
42	  name: default
43	PRESEED
44	fi
45	
46	# ─── download Qdrant on the host ──────────────────────────────────────────────
47	
48	QDRANT_TMP=$(mktemp -d)
49	trap "rm -rf $QDRANT_TMP" EXIT
50	
51	if [[ ! -f "$QDRANT_TMP/qdrant" ]]; then
52	    log "Downloading Qdrant ${QDRANT_VERSION} ..."
53	    curl -fL "$QDRANT_URL" | tar -xz -C "$QDRANT_TMP"
54	fi
55	
56	log "Qdrant binary: $(file $QDRANT_TMP/qdrant | cut -d: -f2 | xargs)"
57	
58	# ─── create container (no NIC) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
59	
60	if incus info "$CONTAINER" &>/dev/null; then
61	    log "Container '$CONTAINER' already exists — stopping and recreating"
62	    incus stop "$CONTAINER" --force 2>/dev/null || true
63	    incus delete "$CONTAINER"
64	fi
65	
66	log "Creating container '$CONTAINER' (Alpine 3.20, no NIC)"
67	
68	# Launch with default profile to get storage, then strip the NIC
69	incus launch images:alpine/3.20 "$CONTAINER" \
70	    --storage "$STORAGE_POOL" \
71	    --no-profiles \
72	    -d root,path=/,pool="$STORAGE_POOL",size=4GiB
73	
74	# Give Alpine a moment to boot
75	sleep 3
76	
77	# ─── add Unix socket proxy BEFORE removing NIC ────────────────────────────────
78	# Incus proxy: host listens on /run/qdrant.sock, bridges to container TCP 6334.
79	# Xray's ds outbound then proxies 127.0.0.1:$QDRANT_PORT → /run/qdrant.sock
80	# via UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS=qdrant:/run/qdrant.sock:$QDRANT_PORT.
81	
82	SOCKET_PATH="/run/qdrant.sock"
83	
84	incus config device add "$CONTAINER" qdrant proxy \
85	    listen=unix:"$SOCKET_PATH" \
86	    connect=tcp:127.0.0.1:6334 \
87	    bind=host
88	
89	log "Proxy device: $SOCKET_PATH -> container:6334 (xray ds outbound will use this)"
90	
91	# ─── install Qdrant inside the container ──────────────────────────────────────
92	
93	log "Pushing Qdrant binary into container"
94	incus file push "$QDRANT_TMP/qdrant" "$CONTAINER/usr/local/bin/qdrant" --mode 0755
95	
96	log "Configuring Qdrant"
97	incus exec "$CONTAINER" -- mkdir -p /var/lib/qdrant /etc/qdrant
98

100	storage:
101	  # Qdrant's storage root must contain collections/ directly. The host mount
102	  # for this system is /var/lib/qdrant/storage, which contains
103	  # collections/repomix_rag.
104	  storage_path: /var/lib/qdrant/storage
105	
106	service:
107	  host: 127.0.0.1
108	  http_port: 6333
109	  grpc_port: 6334
110	  enable_cors: true
111	
112	cluster:
113	  enabled: false
114	
115	telemetry_disabled: true

#!/bin/bash
# Setup Qdrant in an Incus container with no NIC, exposed via a single
# Unix socket at /run/qdrant.sock (gRPC port 6334).
#
# Usage: sudo bash deploy/setup-qdrant-incus.sh
set -euo pipefail

CONTAINER="qdrant"
QDRANT_VERSION="v1.18.1"
QDRANT_URL="https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/releases/download/${QDRANT_VERSION}/qdrant-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz"
STORAGE_POOL="default"
# Local gRPC port — xray proxies 127.0.0.1:$QDRANT_PORT → container via ds transport.
QDRANT_PORT=6334

log() { echo "[qdrant-setup] $*"; }
die() { echo "[qdrant-setup] ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

# ─── preflight ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die "Run as root: sudo bash $0"
command -v incus &>/dev/null || die "incus not found"

# Initialise Incus storage if this is a fresh system
if ! incus storage list --format csv 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    log "Initialising Incus with default storage pool (dir backend)"
    incus admin init --preseed <<'PRESEED'
config: {}
networks: []
storage_pools:
- config: {}
  description: ""
  name: default
  driver: dir
profiles:
- config: {}
  description: ""
  devices:
    root:
      path: /
      pool: default
      type: disk
  name: default
PRESEED
fi

# ─── download Qdrant on the host ──────────────────────────────────────────────

QDRANT_TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap "rm -rf $QDRANT_TMP" EXIT

if [[ ! -f "$QDRANT_TMP/qdrant" ]]; then
    log "Downloading Qdrant ${QDRANT_VERSION} ..."
    curl -fL "$QDRANT_URL" | tar -xz -C "$QDRANT_TMP"
fi

log "Qdrant binary: $(file $QDRANT_TMP/qdrant | cut -d: -f2 | xargs)"

# ─── create container (no NIC) ────────────────────────────────────────────────

if incus info "$CONTAINER" &>/dev/null; then
    log "Container '$CONTAINER' already exists — stopping and recreating"
    incus stop "$CONTAINER" --force 2>/dev/null || true
    incus delete "$CONTAINER"
fi

log "Creating container '$CONTAINER' (Alpine 3.20, no NIC)"

# Launch with default profile to get storage, then strip the NIC
incus launch images:alpine/3.20 "$CONTAINER" \
    --storage "$STORAGE_POOL" \
    --no-profiles \
    -d root,path=/,pool="$STORAGE_POOL",size=4GiB

# Give Alpine a moment to boot
sleep 3

# ─── add Unix socket proxy BEFORE removing NIC ────────────────────────────────
# Incus proxy: host listens on /run/qdrant.sock, bridges to container TCP 6334.
# Xray's ds outbound then proxies 127.0.0.1:$QDRANT_PORT → /run/qdrant.sock
# via UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS=qdrant:/run/qdrant.sock:$QDRANT_PORT.

SOCKET_PATH="/run/qdrant.sock"

incus config device add "$CONTAINER" qdrant proxy \
    listen=unix:"$SOCKET_PATH" \
    connect=tcp:127.0.0.1:6334 \
    bind=host

log "Proxy device: $SOCKET_PATH -> container:6334 (xray ds outbound will use this)"

# ─── install Qdrant inside the container ──────────────────────────────────────

log "Pushing Qdrant binary into container"
incus file push "$QDRANT_TMP/qdrant" "$CONTAINER/usr/local/bin/qdrant" --mode 0755

log "Configuring Qdrant"
incus exec "$CONTAINER" -- mkdir -p /var/lib/qdrant /etc/qdrant

incus exec "$CONTAINER" -- sh -c 'cat > /etc/qdrant/config.yaml' <<'CONF'
storage:
  # Qdrant's storage root must contain collections/ directly. The host mount
  # for this system is /var/lib/qdrant/storage, which contains
  # collections/repomix_rag.
  storage_path: /var/lib/qdrant/storage

service:
  host: 127.0.0.1
  http_port: 6333
  grpc_port: 6334
  enable_cors: true

cluster:
  enabled: false

telemetry_disabled: true
CONF

# ─── OpenRC service ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

incus exec "$CONTAINER" -- sh -c 'cat > /etc/init.d/qdrant' <<'INIT'
#!/sbin/openrc-run

name="qdrant"
description="Qdrant vector database"

command="/usr/local/bin/qdrant"
command_args="--config-path /etc/qdrant/config.yaml"
command_background="yes"
pidfile="/run/qdrant.pid"
output_log="/var/log/qdrant.log"
error_log="/var/log/qdrant.log"

depend() {
    need localmount
    after bootmisc
}
INIT

incus exec "$CONTAINER" -- chmod +x /etc/init.d/qdrant
incus exec "$CONTAINER" -- rc-update add qdrant default
incus exec "$CONTAINER" -- rc-service qdrant start

# ─── verify Qdrant is up inside the container ─────────────────────────────────

log "Waiting for Qdrant to start..."
for i in $(seq 1 15); do
    if incus exec "$CONTAINER" -- wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:6333/healthz 2>/dev/null | grep -q ok; then
        log "Qdrant is healthy inside the container"
        break
    fi
    sleep 1
done

# ─── remove NIC (container is now sealed, no network) ────────────────────────

log "Removing container NIC (sealing network)"
# Alpine has eth0 added by default profile; remove any NIC devices
for dev in eth0 eth1 enp0 enp1; do
    incus config device remove "$CONTAINER" "$dev" 2>/dev/null && \
        log "  Removed NIC: $dev" || true
done

# ─── set socket permissions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The proxy device creates the socket as root; make it group-accessible
SOCKET_GID=$(id -g jeremy 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
chown root:"$SOCKET_GID" "$SOCKET_PATH" 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 660 "$SOCKET_PATH" 2>/dev/null || true

# ─── test connectivity from host via Unix socket ──────────────────────────────

log "Testing gRPC health via Unix socket..."
if command -v grpc_health_probe &>/dev/null; then
    grpc_health_probe -addr unix:"$SOCKET_PATH" && log "gRPC health OK" || true
else
    # Fall back to socat + HTTP check
    if command -v socat &>/dev/null; then
        result=$(echo -e "GET /healthz HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: localhost\r\n\r\n" \
            | socat - UNIX-CONNECT:"$SOCKET_PATH" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 || true)
        log "Socket check: ${result:-no HTTP response (gRPC-only socket is normal)}"
    fi
fi

# ─── summary ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

echo ""
echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo " Qdrant ${QDRANT_VERSION} installed in Incus container '${CONTAINER}'"
echo " Unix socket      : ${SOCKET_PATH}  (Incus proxy → container:6334)"
echo " Container NIC    : none (sealed)"
echo " Storage          : /var/lib/qdrant/storage (inside container)"
echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo ""
echo " Xray routes 127.0.0.1:${QDRANT_PORT} → ${SOCKET_PATH} via ds outbound."
echo " Set in your xray environment:"
echo "   UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS=qdrant:${SOCKET_PATH}:${QDRANT_PORT}"
echo ""
echo " rag-ingest / cognitive-mcp connects to:"
echo "   COGNITIVE_MCP_QDRANT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:${QDRANT_PORT}  (default)"
echo ""
echo " Check status:"
echo "   incus exec ${CONTAINER} -- rc-service qdrant status"
echo "   incus exec ${CONTAINER} -- wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:6333/collections"

content.text: Root cause: the incus **`default` pool is on `/dev/loop0`, only 30 GiB and 100% full** (shared by all containers). But the bind-mounted `/var/lib/cozo` is on `/dev/sda3` with **194 GiB free**. So I'll run cozo entirely from the bind-mount (binary + rocksdb data on sda3), keeping the full loop0 root out of the path. First reclaim the partial push, then host-copy the binary onto the roomy mount:

input.command:
sudo incus exec cozo -- rm -f /usr/local/bin/cozo 2>&1; echo "removed partial"
sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/cozo/bin /var/lib/cozo/db
sudo cp /tmp/claude-1000/-home-jeremy-git-operation-dbus-proto/3ca0a095-5df2-4d79-8fb0-66bbaf96235f/scratchpad/cozo /var/lib/cozo/bin/cozo
sudo chmod 0755 /var/lib/cozo/bin/cozo
echo "=== verify binary runs inside container (on bind-mount) ==="; sudo incus exec cozo -- /var/lib/cozo/bin/cozo server --help 2>&1 | head -5

ExecStart=/var/lib/cozo/bin/cozo server -e rocksdb -p /var/lib/cozo/db/cozo.db -b 127.0.0.1 -P 9070
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=2

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

sudo incus exec cozo -- systemctl enable --now cozo.service 2>&1

content.text:
Found it — and it's first-party, self-describing, and already on disk. RocksDB's **official structured data** comes in two authoritative surfaces, both emitted by rocksdb itself (same pattern as qdrant's OpenAPI and cozo's docs):

## 1. The `OPTIONS-*` file = the canonical *config* schema
RocksDB 8.8.1 persists a versioned, self-documenting INI in the db dir (`/var/lib/cozo/db/cozo.db/data/OPTIONS-000009`). Its header even points to the official format spec (`examples/rocksdb_option_file_example.ini`). It has exactly **four sections** — that's the plugin schema's top-level shape:

| Section | What it carries |
|---|---|
| `[Version]` | `rocksdb_version=8.8.1`, `options_file_version=1.1` |
| `[DBOptions]` | ~70 DB-level options (`max_background_jobs`, `bytes_per_sync`, `wal_recovery_mode`, `create_if_missing`, `max_open_files`, …) |
| `[CFOptions "default"]` | column-family: `compaction_style=kCompactionStyleLevel`, `compression=kLZ4Compression`, `bottommost_compression=kZSTD`, `write_buffer_size`, `num_levels=7`, level triggers, bloom, blob, TTL … |
| `[TableOptions/BlockBasedTable "default"]` | block-based table: block size, cache, filter policy … |

This is authoritative, machine-generated, and **versioned** — ideal as the schema source.

## 2. RocksDB `DB::Properties` (`rocksdb.*`) = the live *runtime* schema
The official `rocksdb.*` property set (`rocksdb.stats`, `rocksdb.levelstats`, `rocksdb.num-files-at-level<N>`, `rocksdb.estimate-num-keys`, `rocksdb.sstables`, `rocksdb.cur-size-all-mem-tables`, compaction/IO stats). That's the operational structured data.

## How this becomes the `rocksdb` plugin
A `rocksdb` StatePlugin (`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/rocksdb.rs`), schema derived from those four OPTIONS sections (config) + the `rocksdb.*` properties (live stats). Live state = parse the on-disk `OPTIONS-*` INI from the cozo db dir + read the DB properties. That makes the **storage engine itself schema-surfaced** — fits "plugin = schema." Roles split cleanly: **cozo plugin** = the Datalog/structured-data query surface; **rocksdb plugin** = the engine config/observability surface beneath it.

This is genuinely part of the same structured-data scope, so it should fold into the spec Kiro is generating (which just finished — I still need to review it). 

Where I've landed this turn: cozo **installed & functional** (rocksdb-backed, Datalog queries work; port quirk noted), rocksdb's authoritative structured data **located**. Want me to (a) build the `rocksdb` plugin now from the OPTIONS schema, and/or (b) review the generated spec and fold the rocksdb plugin into it? Both are queued — say the order.
